mainWord.definition: Having more than one possible meaning.

lessons.mainWordForms: Ambiguous is an adjective. Having more than one possible meaning. His answer was ambiguous, so no one knew what he meant.
lessons.expression: His answer was ambiguous, so no one knew what he meant.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about unclear words.
lessons.expressionTask: Daniel talks to Maya about words and meaning. What does he ask her?
lessons.grammar: Third conditional: If the speaker had chosen clear words, we would have understood him

lessons.task: If the speaker had chosen clear words, we would have ___ him.
lessons.example: If the speaker had chosen clear words, we would have understood him.
context: Daniel talks to Maya about words and meaning at work.
His answer was ambiguous, so no one knew what he meant.
dialogue: Daniel: Maya, what does ambiguous mean?
Maya: It means a word can have more than one meaning.
Daniel: And what is a nuance?
Maya: A nuance is a small difference in meaning.
Daniel: Why was his plan vague?
Maya: He did not get his point across. In a nutshell, we need clear words.
lessons.listening: On Monday, Daniel talks to Maya. He asks, 'Maya, what does ambiguous mean?' Maya says, 'It means a word can have more than one meaning.' Daniel asks, 'And what is a nuance?' Maya says, 'A nuance is a small difference in meaning.' Daniel asks, 'Why was his plan vague?' Maya says, 'He did not get his point across. In a nutshell, we need clear words.'
lessons.question: What does ambiguous mean?
lessons.reading: On Monday, Daniel talks to Maya about words and meaning at Carter Retail Group. He says, 'Maya, what does ambiguous mean?' Maya says, 'It means a word can have more than one meaning. His answer was ambiguous, so no one knew what he meant.' Daniel says, 'And what is a nuance?' Maya says, 'A nuance is a small difference in meaning. A good speaker knows the nuance of each word.' Daniel says, 'Why was his plan vague?' Maya says, 'His plan was vague because he did not get his point across. In a nutshell, we need clear words and short sentences.' Daniel says, 'That is true. If the speaker had chosen clear words, we would have understood him. Vague words waste time, and clear words save time.' Maya says, 'Yes. Words have power, and a small nuance can change a whole talk.'
lessons.readingA: He did not get his point across.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about words and meaning. What does ambiguous mean?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to tell you about words and meaning. On Monday, Daniel talked about words and meaning. He said, 'What does ambiguous mean?' Maya said, 'It means a word can have more than one meaning.' A nuance is a small difference in meaning. His plan was vague because he did not get his point across. In a nutshell, we need clear words.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about words and meaning.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about words and meaning. On Monday, Daniel talked about words and meaning at work. He said, 'What does ambiguous mean?' Maya said, 'It means a word can have more than one meaning.' A nuance is a small difference in meaning. His plan was vague because he did not get his point across. In a nutshell, we need clear words and short sentences. Please tell me about words in your language. Best, Daniel
lessons.sound: Ambiguous has its strongest beat on BIG. In ambiguous, say BIG clearly in the middle. In nuance, say NU clearly at the start.
lessons.model: His answer was ambiguous, so no one knew what he meant.

Let us get straight to the point.
dialogue: Daniel: Maya, what does misinterpret mean?
Maya: It means to understand something in the wrong way.
Daniel: Did he misread the sign?
Maya: Yes, he misread the sign and took the wrong road.
Daniel: Why do you beat around the bush?
Maya: I do not beat around the bush. Let us get straight to the point. Do not miss the point.

Daniel asks, 'Did he misread the sign?' Maya says, 'Yes, he misread the sign and took the wrong road.' Daniel asks, 'Why do you beat around the bush?' Maya says, 'I do not beat around the bush.'
lessons.question: What does misinterpret mean?
lessons.correct: To understand something in the wrong way
lessons.reading: On Thursday, Daniel talks to Maya about a misunderstanding at Carter Retail Group. He says, 'Maya, what does misinterpret mean?' Maya says, 'It means to understand something in the wrong way. The message was misunderstood by the whole team.' Daniel says, 'Did he misread the sign?' Maya says, 'Yes, he misread the sign and took the wrong road.' Daniel says, 'Why do you beat around the bush?' Maya says, 'I do not beat around the bush. Let us get straight to the point. context: Priya talks to Daniel about polite language at work.
She handled the news with great tact.
dialogue: Priya: Daniel, what does blunt mean?
Daniel: It means direct and honest, sometimes too direct.
Priya: What is tact?
Daniel: Tact is skill in dealing with people. She handled the news with great tact.
Priya: Should I hold my tongue in the meeting?

She handled the news with great tact. It might be better to say it more gently.' Priya says, 'Should I hold my tongue in the meeting?' Daniel says, 'Yes. context: Emma talks about language with her mother.
Tell me in plain English what it means.
dialogue: Emma: Mum, what is sarcasm?
Mother: It is saying the opposite of what you mean to mock someone.
Emma: What is irony?
Mother: Irony is saying the opposite of what you mean, often as a joke.
Emma: What does figurative mean?
Mother: It means using words in a picture way. She hit the nail on the head. Tell me in plain English what it means.

lessons.reading: On Monday, Emma talks about language with her mother. Emma says, 'Mum, what is sarcasm?' Her mother says, 'It is saying the opposite of what you mean to mock someone. His sarcasm made the room laugh.' Emma says, 'What is irony?' Her mother says, 'Irony is saying the opposite of what you mean, often as a joke. The irony was that the fire station caught fire.' Emma says, 'What does figurative mean?' Her mother says, 'It means using words in a picture way, not the exact way. She hit the nail on the head with her remark. Tell me in plain English what it means.' Emma says, 'Good. Words can build a bridge, and words can build a wall. I want my words to build a bridge.' Her mother says, 'Yes. A clear word is a gift, and a kind word is a gift too.'
